# Line chart (`line_chart`)

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs.js from schema.json. Edit the schema, then run `npm run docs`. -->

Shows how one or more measures change over a run of time periods, with visible gaps where a period has no data.

**Use when:** A trend over time with more than 8 periods, or any time series with missing or withheld periods: monthly margin, weekly revenue, backorder aging over time.

**Don't use when:** The categories aren't time periods (use bar_chart), there are 8 or fewer periods and exact heights matter (use bar_chart), or there is one current number (use kpi, or gauge against a target).

**Sizes:** M, L, full (default)

## Fields

Fields from `id` to `note` are shared by every widget.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"line_chart"` | yes | Always "line_chart". |
| `id` | string | yes | Unique id within the dashboard: lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, e.g. "open-ar". |
| `title` | string | yes | What the widget shows, in sentence case with no trailing period, e.g. "Revenue by rep, Q3 2026". |
| `subtitle` | string |  | Optional one line of context under the title: scope, filter, or unit. |
| `size` | `"M"` \| `"L"` \| `"full"` |  | Width on the 12-column grid (S = 3, M = 6, L = 9, full = 12). Allowed: M, L, full. Default: `"full"`. |
| `note` | string |  | Optional footnote: caveats, definitions, or why data is missing. |
| `periods` | list of string | yes | Period labels, oldest first, one per period with no periods skipped, e.g. ["Sep 2025", "Oct 2025", ...]. Keep a period whose data is missing and use null for its values, so the gap shows. |
| `series` | list of object | yes | One entry per line. Each series has exactly one value per period, in the same order as periods. |
| `series[].name` | string | yes | Series name shown in the legend and tooltip, e.g. "SLED". |
| `series[].values` | list of number or null | yes | Raw numbers aligned with periods. Use null for a missing or withheld period, never 0: null draws a gap in the line. |
| `format` | `"number"` \| `"integer"` \| `"currency"` \| `"percent"` |  | How values are displayed on the axis and tooltip. percent expects fractions: 0.124 shows as 12.4%. Default: `"number"`. |
| `area` | boolean |  | Shade the area under each line. Use for one or two series that are volumes (revenue, units), not rates. Default: `false`. |
| `reference_lines` | list of object |  | Optional dashed horizontal lines for a threshold or target, in the same format as the values, e.g. [{"label": "Policy floor", "value": 0.08}]. |
| `reference_lines[].label` | string | yes | What the line marks, e.g. "KPA floor" or "Quota". |
| `reference_lines[].value` | number | yes | Where the line sits, as a raw number in the chart's format. |

## Example

```json
{
  "type": "line_chart",
  "id": "margin-by-month",
  "title": "Gross margin by month, Sep 2025 to Oct 2026",
  "subtitle": "Commercial and SLED",
  "size": "full",
  "format": "percent",
  "periods": ["Sep 2025", "Oct 2025", "Nov 2025", "Dec 2025", "Jan 2026", "Feb 2026", "Mar 2026", "Apr 2026", "May 2026", "Jun 2026", "Jul 2026", "Aug 2026", "Sep 2026", "Oct 2026"],
  "series": [
    { "name": "Commercial", "values": [0.121, 0.118, 0.126, 0.131, 0.114, null, null, 0.122, 0.127, 0.133, 0.129, 0.124, 0.137, 0.141] },
    { "name": "SLED", "values": [0.094, 0.089, 0.097, 0.102, 0.088, null, null, 0.091, 0.086, 0.079, 0.083, 0.092, 0.098, 0.101] }
  ],
  "reference_lines": [{ "label": "Policy floor", "value": 0.08 }],
  "note": "Feb and Mar 2026 are withheld while the cost restatement is under review."
}
```

## Checks beyond the schema

- Error when a series has a different number of values than there are periods.
- Error when two series share a name.
- Warns when percent values or reference lines look like whole numbers (45 instead of 0.45).
- Warns when a series has no values at all.
- Warns when there are fewer than 4 periods (use bar_chart).
- Warns when area is true with more than 2 series (overlapping areas hide each other).
